before.known: It is not easy to write and think at the same time when you are learning something new
before.target: Es ist nicht leicht gleichzeitig zu schreiben und nachzudenken wenn du etwas lernen willst

after.known: It is not easy to write and think at the same time when you want to learn something

problem: Meaning: different condition and omitted newness
evidence: English says when you are learning something new; German says wenn du etwas lernen willst, when you want to learn something.

before.known: If you do not mind I want to tell you what I think about this very interesting and good story
before.target: Wenn es dir nichts ausmacht will ich dir sagen was ich über die sehr interessante Geschichte denke

after.known: If you do not mind I want to tell you what I think about this very interesting story

problem: Meaning: English adds an unsupported quality
evidence: The German describes die sehr interessante Geschichte, the very interesting story; English additionally calls it good.

before.known: I'm trying learning German
before.target: Ich versuche Deutsch zu lernen

problem: R8: ungrammatical English infinitive complement
evidence: For an attempt, try takes to learn. Trying learning denotes experimenting with an activity and does not match Ich versuche Deutsch zu lernen.

before.known: I want learning German
before.target: Ich will Deutsch lernen

problem: R8: ungrammatical English; missing LEGO in target
evidence: I want learning German is not a grammatical prompt for Ich will Deutsch lernen. The row also lacks the LEGO Deutsch zu lernen; a known-side repair alone cannot restore containment.

before.known: I know it is fun to practice German very often if you really want to become very good at speaking it
before.target: Ich weiß es macht Spaß sehr oft Deutsch zu üben wenn du sehr gut werden willst

after.known: I know it is fun to practice German very often if you want to become very good

problem: Meaning: English adds speaking and emphasis
evidence: German ends wenn du sehr gut werden willst, if you want to become very good; it does not express really or at speaking it.

before.known: It is important to take time to test yourself when you are learning German with your friends every day
before.target: Es ist wichtig sich Zeit zu nehmen um sich selbst zu testen wenn du Deutsch mit Freunden lernst

after.known: It is important to take time to test yourself when you are learning German with friends

problem: Meaning: everyday frequency omitted
evidence: English says every day; German ends wenn du Deutsch mit Freunden lernst without a frequency expression.

before.known: I think it is important to take time to test yourself again and again when you are practicing something new
before.target: Ich denke es ist wichtig sich Zeit zu nehmen um sich selbst zu testen wenn du etwas üben willst

after.known: I think it is important to take time to test yourself when you want to practise something

problem: Meaning: repetition, newness and aspect differ
evidence: German says wenn du etwas üben willst, when you want to practise something. It does not say again and again or something new.

before.known: Why do you want to stop talking with me when you know I can help you learn German very well today?
before.target: Warum willst du aufhören mit mir zu sprechen wenn du weißt dass ich dir helfen kann Deutsch lernen

problem: Grammar and meaning: broken German complement and omitted details
evidence: The ending helfen kann Deutsch lernen lacks the required infinitive construction here; English also adds very well today without a German equivalent. Compare the grammatical helfen Deutsch zu lernen in seed 61.

before.known: Why do you want to stop reading this very interesting story before you understand what happens in the end?
before.target: Warum willst du aufhören die sehr interessante Geschichte zu lesen bevor du verstehst was passiert

after.known: Why do you want to stop reading this very interesting story before you understand what happens?

problem: Meaning: in the end omitted
evidence: English asks about understanding what happens in the end; German stops at bevor du verstehst was passiert, before you understand what happens.

before.known: Why do you want to stop trying to speak German when you are getting better at speaking it often now?
before.target: Warum willst du aufhören zu versuchen Deutsch zu sprechen wenn du oft besser wirst

problem: R8 and meaning: incoherent improvement clause
evidence: Getting better at speaking it often now is not a clear natural condition. German wenn du oft besser wirst means when you often improve and drops speaking it and now.

before.known: I don't know what to ask about
before.target: Ich weiß nicht, wonach

problem: Meaning: English clause missing in target
evidence: Ich weiß nicht, wonach only supplies I do not know what ... about; the BUILD prompt already includes to ask about, which has no German counterpart. B05 supplies the full fragen soll construction.

before.known: What is he asking about?
before.target: Wonach will er fragen

after.known: What does he want to ask about?

problem: Meaning: intention substituted for action
evidence: Wonach will er fragen asks what he wants to ask about, not what he is asking about.

before.known: I want to know what to ask about
before.target: Ich will wissen, wonach

problem: Meaning: English clause missing in target
evidence: Ich will wissen, wonach stops before the asking clause, but English already includes to ask about. B05 shows the full subordinate clause.

before.known: What are you looking for?
before.target: Was suchst du

problem: R1: course-wide ZUT collision
evidence: The export groups this prompt with seed 194 BUILD S0194L01B01, whose target is Wonach suchst du. Both German forms are grammatical synonyms; standardise this BUILD to the existing target, retaining its LEGO suchst du.

before.known: Thank you very much, but I have got more to learn so I must try
before.target: Vielen Dank, aber ich habe noch mehr zu lernen also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The row ends with muss ich versuchen or werde ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. Unlike English try, bare versuchen does not complete the intended clause here; siblings with complete verbs do not have this defect.

before.known: Thank you very much for helping me to understand so I must try
before.target: Vielen Dank, dass du mir geholfen hast zu verstehen also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The row ends with muss ich versuchen or werde ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. Unlike English try, bare versuchen does not complete the intended clause here; siblings with complete verbs do not have this defect.

before.known: Thank you very much for helping me to understand, but later I will try
before.target: Vielen Dank, dass du mir geholfen hast zu verstehen, aber später werde ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The row ends with muss ich versuchen or werde ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. Unlike English try, bare versuchen does not complete the intended clause here; siblings with complete verbs do not have this defect.

before.known: I am very happy with that so I must try
before.target: Ich bin sehr zufrieden damit also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The row ends with muss ich versuchen or werde ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. Unlike English try, bare versuchen does not complete the intended clause here; siblings with complete verbs do not have this defect.

before.known: I do not understand what you said so I must try
before.target: Ich verstehe nicht, was du gesagt hast also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The row ends with muss ich versuchen or werde ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. Unlike English try, bare versuchen does not complete the intended clause here; siblings with complete verbs do not have this defect.

before.known: Thank you very much, but I have got more to learn, but I need to know
before.target: Vielen Dank, aber ich habe noch mehr zu lernen, aber ich muss es wissen

problem: R8: malformed repeated contrast
evidence: Thank you very much, but I have got more to learn, but I need to know chains two opposing but clauses without a clear relationship. The seed is a natural single contrast; this added tail makes the USE prompt context-dependent.

before.known: Have you got more to learn and that is okay?
before.target: Hast du noch mehr zu lernen und das ist okay

problem: R8: declarative tail grafted onto question
evidence: Have you got more to learn and that is okay? mixes an interrogative with an unframed assertion. German likewise joins Hast du ... und das ist okay without forming a coherent question.

before.known: Have you got more to learn, so you will ask later?
before.target: Hast du noch mehr zu lernen, also wirst du später fragen

problem: R8: malformed question with consequence tail
evidence: Have you got more to learn, so you will ask later? grafts an asserted consequence onto the seed question; German similarly combines a question with also wirst du später fragen.

before.known: Have you got more to learn because I can show you how to do it better?
before.target: Hast du noch mehr zu lernen weil ich dir zeigen kann wie man es besser macht

problem: R8: causal relationship does not support the question
evidence: Have you got more to learn because I can show you how to do it better? makes the speakers ability to demonstrate the cause of the learners having more to learn. It requires substantial invented context, unlike the seed question.

before.known: I am very happy with that, so I will keep trying
before.target: Ich bin sehr zufrieden damit, also werde ich versuchen

problem: Grammar and meaning: keep trying lost
evidence: English says I will keep trying. German ends also werde ich versuchen, an unfinished I will try clause without the continued-action meaning.

before.known: How much I have learnt so I must try
before.target: Wie viel ich gelernt habe also muss ich versuchen

problem: R8: fragment does not extend naturally
evidence: How much I have learnt is a valid subordinate fragment, but adding and that is okay or so I must try leaves it without a governing clause and prevents a natural BUILD continuation. U01 correctly embeds it after I know.

before.known: I am surprised at how quickly I am starting so I must try
before.target: Ich bin überrascht, wie schnell ich anfange also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar: unfinished German versuchen clause
evidence: The target ends also muss ich versuchen without an object or infinitive. The seed completes starting with zu verstehen, whereas this added tail introduces a separate incomplete verb.

before.known: I am surprised at how quickly I am starting, so I must keep trying
before.target: Ich bin überrascht, wie schnell ich anfange, also muss ich versuchen

problem: Grammar and meaning: must keep trying lost
evidence: The target ends also muss ich versuchen, leaving versuchen without its complement and omitting the continued-action meaning of keep trying.

before.known: When did you start to learn and that is okay?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen und das ist okay

problem: R8: declarative tail grafted onto question
evidence: When did you start to learn and that is okay? combines a when question with an unframed assertion; the German has the same incoherent coordination.

before.known: When did you start to learn which I want to know?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen was ich wissen will

problem: R8 and meaning: ambiguous relative attachment
evidence: When did you start to learn which I want to know? is malformed. German was ich wissen will attaches as what I want to know, potentially the object of lernen, rather than clearly asking for the starting time.

before.known: When did you start to learn so I can understand?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen also kann ich verstehen

problem: Meaning: purpose translated as consequence
evidence: English so I can ... supplies a purpose for asking the question. German also kann ich ... asserts a consequence instead. The result is a question followed by a disconnected declarative clause.

before.known: When did you start to learn, so I can learn more?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen, also kann ich mehr lernen

problem: Meaning: purpose translated as consequence
evidence: English so I can ... supplies a purpose for asking the question. German also kann ich ... asserts a consequence instead. The result is a question followed by a disconnected declarative clause.

before.known: When did you start to learn, so I can understand more?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen, also kann ich mehr verstehen

problem: Meaning: purpose translated as consequence
evidence: English so I can ... supplies a purpose for asking the question. German also kann ich ... asserts a consequence instead. The result is a question followed by a disconnected declarative clause.

before.known: When did you start to learn, because I want to know?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen, weil ich wissen will

problem: Grammar and R8: incomplete reason clause
evidence: German weil ich wissen will omits what the speaker wants to know; English because I want to know is also an awkward causal attachment to when did you start. The seed is a clean question without this tail.

before.known: When did you start to learn, I will ask you later?
before.target: Wann hast du angefangen zu lernen, ich werde dich später fragen

problem: R8: incompatible speech acts in one question
evidence: When did you start to learn, I will ask you later? splices a direct question with a promise to ask it later. It is not a natural complete USE prompt; German duplicates the splice.

before.known: I'm not sure when we'll be ready and so we can start
before.target: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, wann wir bereit sein werden, damit wir anfangen können

problem: R8 and meaning: malformed English and changed subject
evidence: Im not sure when well be ready and so we can start is not a coherent English sentence. German damit wir anfangen können expresses purpose, not and so; both sides also switch the LEGO from I to we.
